newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers in alleged ski holiday scam.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers in alleged ski holiday scam.

text.p: The Israeli army suspects a travel agent won dozens of soldiers time off for ski holidays abroad by tricking commanding officers into giving them passes as top athletes.

"Military police, in cooperation with civil police, have opened an investigation into suspicions the soldiers went abroad after purportedly presenting documents that they were top athletes," an army spokesman said on Thursday.

Israel's Itim news agency said police arrested a travel agent believed to have written bogus letters from the Israeli Ski Instructors Association to the army claiming the troops were part of a youth ski team going on week-long training courses.
The army gives "top athletes" time off to hone their skills during their military service. Male conscripts serve for three years and women for 20 months.
Itim said 53 soldiers are suspected of involvement in the alleged scam over a period of several years and each paid the travel agent $1,600 for the vacation "package".

Police began the investigation after the real ski instructors' association discovered its letterhead was being forged, the news agency said. The report did not name the countries where the soldiers went on holiday.
